commits.subject: test(TC-68): fix-2 — pin the BOUND: the honest marker already serves the drift
docs(TC-68): fix-2 GREEN — strike "no new attack surface"; the cache IS cheaper

finding_addressed.disposition: CONCEDED IN FULL. The equivalence argument fix-1 drew from a_forged_stored_baseline_defeats_the_probe_even_when_it_fully_runs is withdrawn. The cache IS a cheaper bypass for an actor who can write the database file. No behaviour changed; the remedy is documentation accuracy plus one new executable assertion.

dominance_claim_3_2.statement: A marker legitimately recorded by an honest earlier open survives a same-identity backend swap and still causes the probe to be skipped, so the drifted backend is served with NO forgery involved. The forgery's incremental capability is therefore confined to opens where no valid marker exists for the CURRENT fingerprint.
verified_against_code: probe_verification_fingerprint (src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:15471) hashes: recipe tag (build const), identity.name/revision/dimension, mean-centering flag + live mean_vec bytes, VECTOR_EQUIVALENCE_PROBE_FIXTURE (build const), the two floors (build consts), and the stored _fathomdb_embed_probe rows. A same-identity backend swap moves none of them: the triple is unchanged by definition (and check_embedder_profile refuses the open outright if it changes), mean_vec/baseline live in the DB and are untouched by swapping backends, the rest are compiled in.
probe_check_against_baseline_inner consults the cache after the fix-2 completeness validation and before the 45 re-embeds; a hit returns Ok(()) with zero model invocations.
dominance_claim_3_2.test_strengthened_in_fix_2: It now reads the marker written by the honest population open BEFORE the drifted open (assert Some), and asserts it is byte-unchanged AFTER (assert_eq against the honest value). No forgery appears anywhere in the test, so the dominance is executable rather than asserted in prose.
dominance_claim_3_2.no_new_test_added_because: The claim was already pinned behaviourally by that test; fix-2 only made the 'honest marker, no forgery' half explicit. The complementary window (forgery on an open with no valid marker) remains pinned by a_marker_matching_the_current_state_serves_a_drifted_backend.
dominance_claim_3_2.precision_note: The window is not only 'fresh databases'. It is three cases, enumerated in design-note §8.5: (1) never verified under the current fingerprint, incl. a pre-TC-68 DB — with the empty-probe-table sub-case where forgery is pointless because probe_populate_or_check baselines against whatever backend is live (pre-existing 0.8.18 behaviour, verified at lib.rs:15366-15375); (2) the open right after a LEGITIMATE fingerprint change (recomputed mean_vec, fixture edit, recipe bump), which an honest open would re-verify and at which the drift WOULD be caught; (3) an open after a failing verdict cleared the marker. Case 2 is the one that matters: it is the only recurring detection opportunity §6 left standing, and a forged marker removes it.

sentences_struck_and_replacements.struck: **Conclusion: the cache adds no new attack surface.** An actor with write access to the SQLite file already had a shorter route — and can in any case rewrite canonical_nodes, the vector_default vec0 rows and _fathomdb_embedder_profiles.mean_vec directly... The probe was never a boundary against that actor; the cache changes *when* it runs, not *who can lie to it*.
sentences_struck_and_replacements.replacement: "What this establishes, and all it establishes: the same actor already had a route that defeats the probe while it runs in full. It does NOT establish that the two routes cost the same — see §8.4, which is where fix-1 went wrong." plus NEW §8.4 (the cost asymmetry conceded, with codex's own wording quoted and the sentence marked STRUCK) and NEW §8.5 (the bound).

bounded_staleness_verdict.recommendation: AGREE WITH THE ORCHESTRATOR — NOT WORTH IT HERE. Not implemented.
bounded_staleness_verdict.recorded_at: dev/design/0.8.20-tc68-equivalence-probe-fingerprint-cache.md §8.7 (first bullet, 'CONSIDERED, NOT TAKEN; deferred with the trade named'), cross-referenced from §6.2
reasoning: It is the ONLY candidate on the hardening list that buys real coverage — it bounds both the forged marker AND the ruled residual to at most N opens / that age, because the drifted backend is eventually asked to embed. That is stated plainly rather than minimised.

But it partially undoes the property TC-68 was ruled to deliver: constant, predictable Engine::open cost. One open in N pays 45 embeds again and it is not predictable which — the same objection that killed the TTL at §6.2, unchanged by the threat framing.

It needs durable state (counter or timestamp) plus a tuning constant: new surface and a new correctness question (clock skew, reset counter, what N means for a process that opens once and runs for a week) in a slice scoped not to grow surface.

It should be decided against §6.2's backend-descriptor fingerprint input, which RETIRES the residual rather than merely bounding it and needs the same HITL governed-surface decision. Deciding them separately would likely ship both.
bounded_staleness_verdict.escalation: None requested. I did not conclude it is cheap and clearly right; I concluded it is a real option whose cost lands on the exact property this slice exists to deliver. Deferred visibly, with the trade written down, for the batched governed-surface decision the plan places after Slice 22.
